circuits.display_name: Two-stage Miller OTA, fully differential (no CM control)

provenance.notes: A plain-Miller FD OTA with no common-mode control ('no CM control' is the topology's defining feature, not a defect); the resistive CM servo it omits is added by amp_030, which composes this core. Common-source second stage = high output impedance = an OTA (subfamily: ota, drawings/README.md). Deviations from the drawing: the first-stage load-gate net X is FLOATING as drawn — landed as the internal knob source {vbl}; the 1 mA bias literal became the {i_bias} knob (re-seeded to 20 uA). CHARACTERIZATION FINDING (committed as the dc_cm_bias_sweep analysis; tt; refined by the 2026-07 sizing study): with no CM control at either stage, an interior DC point EXISTS but only inside a knife-edge vbl window obeying width x CM-gain ~ 0.5 V — 0.2 mV wide at the 50 dB baseline sizing (0.7086-0.7088), 3.5 mV at a 37 dB min-L sizing, and wide (>0.5 V) only in a degenerate ~3.5 mA regime 7x over the i_supply spec (two cascaded gds-level knife edges; up/down fine sweeps agree — sensitivity, not hysteresis). The committed vbl default is tt-centered to 4 decimals, so dc_gain/pm/ugf/t_settle measure honestly at tt (design 2e55cced7c: 50.5 dB / 77.4 deg / 97 MHz / 3.1 us, all pass); cm_interior_pts stays 0 by design — no gain-spec-compatible sizing widens the window to the bench's 20-30 mV sample spacing, i.e. the robustness fail is the topology, not the sizing. amp_030 composes this core with the resistive CM servo (CMFB) that makes the amplifier usable. Kept (de-published, `published: false`) as the pre-CMFB core that amp_030's composition repairs.

circuits.display_name: Fan CCIA chopper OTA core + real 5T CMFB (COMPOSITE: amp_026 + cmfb_002_5t_pmos_input)

provenance.designer: Composition by Noorizadeh (MacAnalog group); blocks: amp_026 (Fan core, hand-drawn xschem) + cmfb_002_5t_pmos_input (owner 5T CMFB, 2026-07-20 campaign winner)
provenance.notes: The CM-closure answer to doc/review_chopper_cm_rejection_2026-08-04.md. amp_026 has NO CMFB, so its output common mode is a device-ratio knife edge and its CM rejection is structurally poor (ihp-sg13g2 tt baseline: cmrr_cm_corr_db +10.4 dB, psrr_cm_corr_db -2.4 dB). Chopping cannot fix it — the output chopper swaps voutp<->voutn and vocm = (voutp+voutn)/2 is invariant under that swap. This entry closes the CM loop with a REAL (transistor-level) CMFB rather than an ideal servo. ACTUATOR (measured open-loop with the amplifier/dc_cmfb_plant_sign math, not assumed — see composition.yaml): the class-A output PMOS current sources XM8/XM9 are LIFTED OUT of the core's shared {vb4} bias tree and re-instantiated by the composite on their own gate node vb4o. Driving the whole vb4 tree instead is a NON-inverting plant (cm_plant_delta +1.19 V) needing the un-accessioned -inv servo; the split-out output pair alone is INVERTING (-1.06 V) — exactly what the canonical cmfb_00x blocks drive. Tail XM1 and fold sources XM6/XM7 keep the unregulated {vb4}, so the CM correction never modulates the input-pair gm.
provenance.paper: Q. Fan, F. Sebastiano, J. H. Huijsing, K. A. A. Makinwa, "A 1.8 uW 60 nV/sqrt(Hz) Capacitively-Coupled Chopper Instrumentation Amplifier in 65 nm CMOS for Wireless Sensor Nodes", IEEE JSSC 46(7):1534-1543, Jul. 2011 (the CORE only; the CMFB closure is owner work)

circuits.display_name: Fan CCIA chopper OTA + DUAL 5T CMFB (COMPOSITE: amp_026 + 2x cmfb_002_5t_pmos_input)

provenance.designer: Composition by Noorizadeh (MacAnalog group); blocks: amp_026 (Fan core, hand-drawn xschem) + 2x cmfb_002_5t_pmos_input (owner 5T CMFB, 2026-07-20 campaign winner)
provenance.notes: Plan P4-4b SECOND HALF. amp_034_fan_chopper_cmfb closes the OUTPUT common mode and gains +43.4 dB of CM rejection, but leaves stage 1 open — and that residue is measurable: the core's hand-tuned vb1 = 0.398 balances the fold nodes only near a 0.6 V INPUT common mode, so a 0.5 V input CM rails stage 1 and drags the output to ~0.026 V (the BARE core does the same, vocm = 0.004 V). This entry replaces that hand-set knob with a second loop. The stage-1 actuator only became usable once amp_034 existed: in the bare core {vb4} gates the tail AND the fold sources AND the output sources, making it a NON-inverting plant (+1.19 V); with XM8/XM9 lifted onto vb4o it is a clean stage-1-only actuator and measures INVERTING (-1.093 V), so the canonical cmfb_00x drives it. Both loops therefore use the canonical block. Loop 2 is forced to the PMOS-input flavor: it senses a 0.327 V common mode, where an NMOS pair would need a negative tail voltage. Its sense resistors are overridden to 50 MOhm so the averager does not load the cascoded stage-1 nodes. See doc/review_amp035_dual_cm_closure_2026-08-05.md.

circuits.display_name: Real 5T CMFB (PMOS-input error amp + resistive CM detector, canonical)

provenance.notes: The first REAL (transistor-level) member of the cmfb class — the drop-in replacement for the ideal CMFB macromodels (identical pin footprint; swapping a consumer is a pure symbol-path change). CANONICAL polarity: PMOS pair puts the sensed CM on the + input, vcmfb = A*(cm_sense - vref) — for INVERTING plants (B5 rule; the -inv wiring variant for non-inverting plants exists in drawings/ shared as cmfb-output-amp-5t-pmos-input-inv, not separately accessioned: same topology, swapped pair gates). Self-biased via an on-cell 2-diode string — the block has NO bias pin, so composition needs no bias plumbing. Chosen (over the NMOS-input flavor, cmfb_003) for the SRMC core consumer: its zero-error natural output sits nearest the plant's actuator balance gates and its PMOS pair is comfortable at the 0.5 V sensed CM. Rail-clamped by construction — in-loop CM kicks recover with zero residual (vs the unclamped macromodel's basin escapes). In-loop validation (sized amp_031 SRMC core, both loops real): CM errors 3.6/2.1 mV, diff 54.72 dB / 76.9 MHz / PM 58.9 deg, 116.4 uA total; consumer drawing SRMC-core-amp-w-cmfb-5t.sch (SIZING_VALIDATION_REPORT.md §8).
provenance.paper: Y.-P. Hsu, S.-L. Liu, M. M. Hella (SRMC bio-AFE context, TCAS-I 67(1) 2020) — the CMFB itself is an owner design replacing the drawn ideal servos

circuits.display_name: Switched-capacitor CMFB (two-phase charge-redistribution CM detector, canonical)

provenance.notes: The class's first SWITCHED-CAPACITOR member — no error amplifier at all: per side, a switched cap alternates between the (vcm, vbias) reference pair on clk_phi and the (vin, vcmfb) sensed/control pair on clk_phi_not, so charge redistribution enforces vcmfb = cm(vinp,vinn) - vcm + vbias in steady state. Discrete-time transfer slope is +1 by construction (CANONICAL polarity, for inverting plants — B5 rule) and the zero-error actuator level equals vbias: PROGRAMMED, not sized (contrast cmfb_002/003, whose vcmfb_nat placement is the sizing problem). This is the Hsu paper's CMFB for the SRMC core amp — the committed amp_031 consumer instead carries the real 5T CMFB (cmfb_002 flavor); swapping it for this network is the composition follow-up (needs the two-phase clock pair plumbed). vcmfb is Hi-Z during the refresh phase — the consumer's actuator gate is the hold capacitance, so the block only regulates into a capacitive load. Clocked-only characterization: the CT class benches (dc_cmfb_transfer/ac_servo) see purely capacitive paths and are meaningless here — the whole suite is the tran_sc_cmfb_step template (class metrics.yaml, 2026-07-27).

provenance.notes: The full Fan architecture the drawn tops omit: the ripple-reduction loop (sup_003) composed around the chopper CCIA (ia_002) — RRL senses the output ripple, demodulates at the output-chopper clock, integrates through a two-phase SC network, and injects the DC correction at the first-stage outputs (pre output chopper). HONEST LIMITATION (2026-07-17 adversarial verify): the composed core has NO common-mode control, so once the RRL's SC clocks actually run, the output CM rails to ~+1.19 V within ~1-2 ms and every clocked transient aborts — so the ripple-nulling figure and the demodulation-sign question (DRAWING_REVIEW §4.2) CANNOT be exercised on this composite. (An earlier v_ripple0_pp "~40x nulling" headline here was measured with the SC clocks accidentally undriven, i.e. the RRL INERT — that bench bug is fixed in the template and the invalid headline removed.) The clocked RRL benches are therefore not bound; the RRL demonstration + demod sign are deferred to the core-CM closure composite (plan P4-4b, cf. amp_030). The static benches (cap-ratio gain, HPF corner, static Zin) are valid and bound.

provenance.designer: Noorizadeh (schematic capture, after Fan et al.)
provenance.notes: Ripple-sensing demodulating SC integrator — the RRL servo of Fan's CCIA (DRAWING_REVIEW S4): Cs AC-couples the main amplifier's output ripple, the internal 4-gate chopper synchronously demodulates it at f_chop, and the auto-zeroed SC core integrates the demodulated product into the correction drive. AC-coupled BY DESIGN — a DC differential input transfers zero net charge per cycle (DC rejection is a feature, not a bug), so the bench is tran_rrl_sense (square ripple at FCHOP + synchronous CLK_CH_RRL), not a DC-ramp integrator bench. The chopper matches the fixed drawing (DRAWING_REVIEW item 1 FIXED): true 4-gate modulator, and the DRAWN clock hookup (Vctl fed from CLK_CH_RRL_not, i.e. straight-leg NMOS gates on clk_ch_rrl_not) is preserved exactly — that assignment sets the demodulation sign of the composed RRL loop (S4.2), recorded as the SIGN of the ripple_gain metric. The drawn TG wiring uses the opposite PHI phase as each switch complement, so the bench drives PHI_1/PHI_2 as exact complements (see tran_rrl_sense header). Entry-level wrap deviations: the drawing's Vb1..Vb4 bias ports become internal knob-driven sources (instantiator owns bias); the ideal-amp leaf's gm_val/rout_val/... symbols match the drawing (normalized at source, DRAWING_REVIEW item 5).
